screens.prompt: In B7, total the North amounts from the sales table in A1:B6.

hints.syntax: =SUMIF(A2:A6,"North",B2:B6): condition range, condition, then the numbers to add.
hints.func-sumif: SUMIF adds only the rows that match. SUM would give the total of every region, which is a different question.
hints.require-ref: The sum range has to be the amount column, not the region column.
hints.value: That is not the North total. With only two arguments SUMIF adds the region names, which is zero.
hints.error: #VALUE! means the criteria and sum ranges are different shapes: A2:A6 and B2:B6 have to line up row for row.

reject.why: no sum range, so SUMIF sums the region names
the ranges are swapped, so it sums the text column
stops before the last North row
adds every region instead of filtering
the region column starts at A3, so A2 is never read and the first North row is skipped
sums the empty column instead of B2:B6

docs.explain:
SUMIF asks two things at once: which rows match, and which column gets added. The regions sit in A2:A6, the condition is North, and the amounts sit in B2:B6.

=SUMIF(A2:A6,"North",B2:B6) returns 900 from the three North rows of 320, 180 and 400, while the table holds 1450. The third argument is the one people drop, and dropping it makes SUMIF add the region names instead, which comes back as 0 with no error to show for it.

Conditions behave as they do in COUNTIF, so ">=200" and "N*" both work. The two ranges are matched by position, so give them the same shape.

errors.text: The sum range and the criteria range are different shapes, so the rows no longer line up.
The function is misspelled, or SUMIFS was used with the argument order SUMIF keeps.
Leaving out the sum range makes SUMIF add the region names. The answer is 0 and Excel reports nothing.

docs.atWork: A flat export turned into a summary by category, without a pivot table.
docs.outcome: Total only the rows that match a region.

seo.title: SUMIF in Excel: total one category
seo.description: SUMIF adds only the rows that match, which is why the third argument matters. Three North rows add to 900 while the whole table holds 1450.
